data.name: Prototype
data.Definition: The second browser app under web/src/prototype that mirrors the four dashboard screens and a design system page against invented data. It is a design reference and is not part of the shipped dashboard.

data.name: Mock data
data.Definition: The invented sessions, rates, sources and totals in the prototype data file, which stand in for the real API response.

data.name: Reference screen
data.Definition: A prototype screen that a developer reads beside the shipped screen it corresponds to, then copies the layout of.

data.name: Design system page
data.Definition: The prototype tab named Design system, a gallery of tokens, controls and domain components, with no counterpart in the shipped dashboard.

data.name: Dashboard developer
data.Description: A person who builds or restyles the dashboard and opens the prototype to see how a screen or component should look.

data.name: The prototype is excluded from the production build
data.Statement: The production build writes to the Python package folder from a single page, and the repository guide states the prototype page is deliberately left out of it.

refs.quote: inside the Python wheel. It must stay working. `prototype.html` is deliberately excluded

data.name: Prototype filters do not filter the screens
data.Statement: The filter rail in the prototype changes its own state and chips, but the screens are rendered without any filter value, so the figures on screen never change.

data.name: Prototype session table shows at most 120 rows
data.Statement: The prototype sorts all sessions and then displays only the first 120.

data.name: Prototype splits session cost across token buckets by fixed weights
data.Statement: The session drawer apportions a session's cost across the four token buckets with constant weights, not with real rates.

data.name: Prototype rescan is staged
data.Statement: The Rescan logs button only shows a scanning state for 900 milliseconds and reads no logs.

data.name: Prototype figures are invented
data.Statement: The headline totals are literal numbers and the session list is generated from a few seed sessions.

data.name: Do not import from the prototype folder
data.Statement: The migration guide tells porters to copy the composition of a prototype screen and never to import from the prototype folder.

refs.quote: from `prototype/` — it is mock data; copy the composition, not the module.

data.name: Compare a dashboard screen with its reference
data.Description: A [[Dashboard developer]] opens the [[Prototype]] page to see how one of the four screens, or a design system part, should look against [[Mock data]], then reads the matching [[Reference screen]] before changing the shipped screen.
data.Preconditions: The Vite development server is running.
data.Postconditions: Nothing is stored; the developer knows the target layout.
Main flow: 1. The developer opens /prototype.html, which loads the prototype entry script. `web/prototype.html:25`
2. The entry script mounts the Prototype shell. `web/src/prototype/main.tsx:9`
3. The developer picks a tab: Overview, Sessions, Sources, Models and pricing, or Design system. `web/src/prototype/Prototype.tsx:16`
4. The shell renders the Design system page for the gallery tab and the Screens component for every other tab. `web/src/prototype/Prototype.tsx:98-107`
5. Screens renders the chosen reference screen from mock data. `web/src/prototype/Screens.tsx:360-368`
6. In Sessions, the developer opens a row to see the session drawer. `web/src/prototype/Screens.tsx:375`
data.Alternative flows: 4a. For the gallery tab the Filters button is hidden. `web/src/prototype/Prototype.tsx:70-79`
data.Acceptance criteria: No test covers the prototype. Criteria come from the code: the page offers five tabs, the Rescan logs button reads no logs, and filters do not change the screens.
data.Special requirements: The prototype is served only by the development server and is not in the production build.

data.name: Prototype looks live but is staged
data.Risk: Filters, the rescan button and the scanned 2 min ago text suggest real behaviour but do nothing, so a reader may take the prototype for working product.
data.Mitigation: Notes state the staged parts; the migration guide marks the folder read only.

data.name: Design system README and migration guide are out of date
data.Risk: The README says the shipped dashboard still runs on the old src/ds CSS system, but the shipped entry point already imports the new theme and the ds folder is absent.
data.Mitigation: Open question for the owner of the web folder; this chunk does not edit those files.

data.name: No tests cover the prototype
data.Risk: No test file imports or lives inside the prototype folder, so a change to a reference screen is unchecked except by typecheck and lint.
data.Mitigation: Accepted: the folder is read only reference code.

data.name: Is the prototype still wanted once every screen is ported?
data.Question: The migration guide treats the folder as a working reference during the port. Should it be deleted or kept after the port, and should the README and guide be updated to say the port is done? Checked web/src/design-system/MIGRATION.md and README.md.
